record.paper_title: The Li–Lin’s open problem on R^N
record.original_question: For an integer N ≥ 3, let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in R^N, let 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, let λ > 0, and define the Hardy–Sobolev critical exponent 2*(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2) for 0 ≤ s ≤ 2. For parameters 2 < p ≤ 2*(s1) and 2 < q ≤ 2*(s2), does the zero-Dirichlet Hardy–Sobolev equation −Δu = −λ |x|^(−s1) |u|^(p−2)u + |x|^(−s2) |u|^(q−2)u in Ω, with u = 0 on ∂Ω, admit positive solutions in the Li–Lin regime s1 < s2 and λ > 0, particularly in the difficult case p > q and especially p > q = 2*(s2)?

evidence.quote: In 2012, Y.Y. Li and C.-S. Lin (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., 203 (3): 943–968) posed an open problem concerning the existence of positive solutions to the elliptic equation { −∆u = −λ|x|−s1 |u|p−2u + |x|−s2 |u|q−2u in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, for λ > 0, p > q = 2∗(s2), 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, and 2∗(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2) denotes the Hardy-Sobolev critical exponent, initially studied in bounded domains Ω ⊂ RN, N ≥ 3. Currently, research on this open problem remains limited, and a complete resolution is still far from being achieved.

Consider the following nonlinear equation involving Hardy-Sobolev exponents: { −∆u = −λ|x|−s1 |u|p−2u + |x|−s2 |u|q−2u in Ω, u(x) = 0 on ∂Ω, (1.1) where ∆ denotes the standard Laplace operator, Ω is a smooth bounded domain in RN (N ≥ 3), λ ∈ R, 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, 2∗(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2) for 0 ≤ s ≤ 2, 2 < p ≤ 2∗(s1), and 2 < q ≤ 2∗(s2).

However, when λ > 0 and p > q, (PS)c sequences may not be bounded, making it difficult to obtain satisfactory results. Y.Y. Li and C.-S. Lin [8] identified this challenge in their research and posed the following open problem: When s1 < s2 and λ > 0, the existence of positive solutions to equation (1.1) remains completely unknown.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N\geq 3$ be an integer and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a smooth bounded domain (containing the origin in the relevant cases). For $0\leq s\leq 2$, define the Hardy–Sobolev critical exponent
$$2^*(s)=\frac{2(N-s)}{N-2}.$$
Fix parameters
$$0\leq s_1<s_2<2,\qquad 2<p\leq 2^*(s_1),\qquad 2<q\leq 2^*(s_2),\qquad \lambda>0,$$
and consider the Dirichlet problem
$$\begin{cases}-\Delta u=-\lambda\,|x|^{-s_1}\,|u|^{p-2}u+|x|^{-s_2}\,|u|^{q-2}u & \text{in }\Omega,\\ u=0 & \text{on }\partial\Omega.\end{cases}$$
Determine whether this problem admits a positive (classical or weak $H^1_0(\Omega)$) solution in the regime $s_1<s_2$ and $\lambda>0$. In particular, settle the case $p>q$, and most notably the critical case $p>q=2^*(s_2)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed by Y.Y. Li and C.-S. Lin (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., 2012), is widely described in the recent literature as still open. Only partial positive answers exist (e.g., Cerami–Zhong–Zou type results, and recent works such as arXiv:2402.12206 published in J. Differential Equations, 2025), but a complete resolution in the difficult regime $\lambda>0$, $p>q=2^*(s_2)$ has not been achieved.
